## What RFind-sc does

RFind-sc scores single cells against **case-vs-control gene panels**. A panel
is a pair of gene lists: UP (case-upregulated) and DOWN (case-downregulated).
Each cell's genes are ranked by the P2 Pearson residual `(obs - exp)/sqrt(exp + 1)`,
and the cell's UP/DOWN lists are compared with the panel's by the Running Fisher
test (smallest hypergeometric p over every top-G × top-K cut-off pair; an
unordered gene set, such as a Hallmark gene group, is used whole and only the
cell's cut-offs are scanned). The
score is **signed**: positive for case-aligned cells, negative for
control-aligned.

This is the complement of tools like AUCell and UCell, which are designed for
directionless pathway scoring (MSigDB Hallmark, GO, etc.) and return
non-negative scores that cannot express direction.

## Quick start

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(RFindsc)
library(Seurat)

mg <- readRDS("path/to/my_microglia_seurat.rds")
out <- run_pipeline(mg, biosets = default_biosets())

# Score matrix: cell x panel (DAM, Maturity, Interferon, G2M)
head(out$scores)
```

## Panels you can use

Three tiers of panel access:

1. **Bundled references of the paper** — `default_biosets()` returns the 4
   Hammond axes (DAM and Maturity signed references; Interferon and G2M
   Hallmark gene groups); `load_dedonno_biosets()` returns the 4 De Donno axes
   (Glucocorticoid, Seizure, UPR, NF-kB).
2. **MSigDB on demand** — `msigdbr_to_panels(species, collection)` pulls any
   MSigDB collection.
3. **Auto-paired CGP** — `c2_cgp_auto_pair(species)` pulls the ~850 MSigDB C2
   CGP panel pairs with `_UP` / `_DN` suffixes and pairs them.

## Building a panel from your own DEG

```{r, eval = FALSE}
deg <- read.csv("my_deg_table.csv")   # cols: gene, log2FC, padj
p <- build_panel_from_deg(deg,
                          gene_col = "gene",
                          log2fc_col = "log2FC",
                          padj_col  = "padj",
                          padj_thresh = 0.05,
                          label = "my_condition")

out <- run_pipeline(mg, biosets = list(my_condition = p))
```

The whole ranked table is kept in the panel; at scoring time it is restricted
to the genes of the dataset and the top `top_n` (500) genes per side are used,
as in the RFind-sc paper.

## Migrating from AUCell

If you already use AUCell, RFind-sc accepts the same input shape as
`AUCell::AUCell_calcAUC()` via `score_genesets()`: a counts matrix (or
Seurat object) plus a named list of gene character vectors.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(RFindsc)

# AUCell-style invocation: same input, drop-in compatible
gene_sets <- list(
  microglia_marker = c("Tmem119", "P2ry12", "Cx3cr1"),
  inflammation     = c("Tnf", "Il1b", "Nfkb1")
)
out <- score_genesets(mg, gene_sets)
head(out$scores)              # cell x set RFind-sc scores
```

`score_genesets()` uses the two-term reduction (DOWN list empty) and treats each
set as unordered (used whole), so it is interchangeable with AUCell on
single-list pathway scoring tasks.
**To use the direction-aware four-term score** (RFind's distinguishing
feature), supply `(UP, DOWN)` panels instead via `score_panel_pairs()`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
panels <- list(
  my_contrast = list(up = case_up_genes, down = case_down_genes)
)
out <- score_panel_pairs(mg, panels)
# scores are now signed: positive = case-aligned, negative = control-aligned
```

For end-to-end use with the bundled references, `run_pipeline()`
remains the single-call entry point.

## Per-cell-type baseline

Each cell's signature is its deviation from a baseline: by default the mean CPM of
all cells. In a dataset with many cell types, cell identity then dominates the
signature. Pass `baseline_groups` (one label per cell) to compare each cell with
the cells of its own group instead, as the RFind-sc paper does for the De Donno
et al. hippocampus (baseline per cell type, both conditions pooled):

```{r, eval = FALSE}
out <- run_pipeline(seu, biosets = load_dedonno_biosets(),
                    baseline_groups = seu$cell_type)
```

## Configuration

Hyperparameters (defaults follow the paper):

```{r, eval = FALSE}
cfg <- rfindsc_config(top_n = 500, n_cell = 500, clip = 300)
out <- run_pipeline(mg, config = cfg)
```
